reason: Pinned §3.2 already requires reserving each returned entry, while both reference hosts ignore consume_nonces in local mode, supporting a narrower consistency finding.
The pinned newline permission conflicts with literal no-trailing-bytes wording, and the fixtures lack whitespace-boundary controls, supporting an explicit framing grammar.
A universal acceptance floor is unspecified, but the existing vector explicitly sets a 65536-byte bound and uses oversize_stdout, weakening the arbitrary-bound premise and proposed classification.

Pinned hosts demonstrably disagree, but the proposed denial vectors reject numbers permitted by the normative [JSON Schema semantics](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-validation#section-6.1.1), requiring compatibility resolution before staging.
Pinned JavaScript supervision kills only the child PID while Rust uses process groups, confirming a cleanup gap whose vector needs descendant readiness and bounded post-timeout observation.
Nonce-less allows are explicitly permitted, and rejecting them universally would change valid behavior without proving that the configured verifier omitted required replay protection.
Pinned prose and schema omit retention lower bounds, allowing premature eviction and replay despite the reference verifier already emitting effectiveExpiry.
Full validation precedes reservation in §10 pseudocode and both hosts, but negative store-mutation coverage is absent and requires extending the runner's assertions.
Pinned request schemas accept extension fields without defining their authorization guarantees, supporting a bounded clarification of host assumptions and documented capability-token bindings.
Pinned fixtures lack detail-bearing denies, making positive and wrong-type controls valuable while preserving detail's documented diagnostic role.
Request digests cannot reconstruct request bytes, and the proposed tuple omits verifier dependencies and mutable replay state, so its byte-identical rerun guarantee is unsupported.

Searches of [CONTINUITY v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.05269v1) found none of the supplied EVC terms or quoted closure language, and the unversioned procedure cannot substantiate the claimed equivalence.
Both missing acceptance controls are confirmed in the actual JavaScript fixtures and test-vectors.json, although the candidate's fixture JSON glob is incorrect.

The pinned draft makes JSON Schema normative without corresponding references, supporting reference additions independently of the unverified idnits prediction and unnecessary prose-precedence clause.

The draft already includes Implementation Status, removal guidance and a pinned external URL, while [RFC 7942](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7942#section-2) permits partial field coverage, leaving narrower URL and coverage improvements.
The pinned IANA section already specifies registration policy, wire-version metadata and closure-preserving registrations, and explicitly explains why kind requires no registry.

A public [implementation](https://github.com/aporthq/aport-agent-guardrails) confirms overlap, but the [paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.20953v1) defers its anonymized dataset and neither independent benchmark reproduction nor EVC adapter compatibility is established.

Documented [HTTP and gRPC external authorization](https://agentgateway.dev/docs/standalone/main/documentation/configuration/security/external-authz/) supports investigating interoperability, but subprocess compatibility, maintainer demand and live repository reconciliation remain unverified.
The [mcp_tool criterion](https://www.pomerium.com/docs/internals/ppl) is documented, but no compatible external-verifier hook or expressed adoption demand supports the proposed fit.

A version-pinned citation check is feasible, but searches of [v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.05269v1) found no supplied EVC terms and its authenticated authorization witness requires substantially more than EVC host conformance.
The commands omit --type host_behavior and select 113 vectors, while successful runner output exposes no failure classes, requiring corrected selection and actual decision capture.
Fixtures are JavaScript files, an existing SHA-256 manifest already passes sync:check, and repository equality cannot establish equality with the published npm tarball.

Pinned mandate issuance creates placeholder Groth16 proofs for classical verification, so the promised bolyra verify allow is unsupported and binding-signature verification alone cannot establish full verifier conformance.

Source inspection shows both historical hosts already contain the tested behavior, while the procedure omits pinned vector selection and successful-class capture, limiting its discriminative evidence.
